title: Ghost reset bisect notes and candidate hypotheses
body:
Context:
- Recurring class of node resets seen since 2027-06 across two racks (rack-a09, rack-a10). Resets manifest as an immediate disconnected worker (lost ssh, node disappears from k8s node list) with no obvious kernel oops in syslog for ~60% of events. The other ~40% show nvlink negotiation errors or sudden correctable ECC burst then driver unload stack traces.
- We nickname these "ghost resets": short-lived reboots or driver reloads where the OS either soft-resets GPU driver stack or host kernel reboots, but metadata (BMC/IPMI) sometimes reports no graceful shutdown.
- Impact: ~0.3% job eviction rate for long-running Dedicated pools; spikes correlate with nightly long sequences of large batch runs.

Data summary (raw signals observed):
- ECC counters: small bursts (10-50 correctables) immediately preceding ~40% of events. Not all nodes with bursts reset.
- nvlink logs: repeated "link training timeout" or "handshake: peer down" messages on 3 occasions; on others, nvlink logs unremarkable.
- driver: nvidia-driver 515.x on affected fleet subset; newer canary driver 520.x on a few nodes where we saw fewer events (not enough sample).
- kernel logs: when present, stack traces include gpu driver panic followed by watchdog reset. In many events, syslog rollover/rsyslog crash time window indicates logs truncated at time of failure.
- PSU / power telemetry: minor voltage sag correlating with heavy concurrent colocation on same PDU in rack-a10 during one-day spike.

Repro attempts so far (summary):
- Workload replay: replayed heavy decode+long context workloads on isolated node for 48h -> one soft-reset after 19h.
- Synthetic ECC stress: memtest-like kernels on GPU memory -> induced correctable bursts but not deterministic resets.
- NVLink stress (=cross-GPU peer traffic) -> increased chance of nvlink message in dmesg but no hard reset.
- Kernel/drivers: switched single node to driver 520.12-rc -> ran 72h no reset (n=1), not statistically significant but suggests driver interacts.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Intermittent power integrity event combined with heavy NVLink traffic -> transient NVLink retry -> driver internal state corruption -> soft unload/reset. Rationale: power sag observed once; power events can manifest as link flaps.
2) Driver / firmware race condition under high concurrency + specific kernel scheduler path -> driver calls into hw while link is mid-retraining -> null pointer/stack corruption -> kernel hang then watchdog. Rationale: stacktraces point at driver code paths for memory release.
3) Memory ECC scrub interacting with host kernel page reclaim -> momentary spike in correctables that trips internal protective path in older firmware -> failover. Rationale: Correctable spikes precede some events.
4) NVLink retimer chip intermittent fault on specific nodes -> only visible in low-level nvlink negotiation logs; other nodes with same hw revision not affected due to silicon variance.
5) Telemetry/logging blind spot: some resets are happening but logs are not flushed due to rsyslog/nginx crashes or dmesg ring overrun. This makes causal inference harder.

Next-phase experiments (actionable & low-risk):
A) Isolate a small test pool (3 nodes) and run continuous workload with full telemetry capture (enable persistent early printk, netconsole to remote collector, enable nvidia debugfs verbose) for 7 days. Goal: capture pre-reset kernel/dmesg. Owner: Diego. Start: 2027-07-20.
B) Controlled power variation test: coordinate with hardware to apply small injected load on PDU to attempt to reproduce sag under NVLink traffic. Safety: on test pool only. Owner: Priya. Start: 2027-07-24 (requires infra maintenance window).
C) Driver bisect: prepare image variants with driver 515.x (baseline), 517.y (known heuristics), and 520.12-rc. Roll each for 72h across matched nodes and compare reset frequency normalized by GPU-hours. Owner: Ethan. Start: 2027-07-21.
D) Add ECC scrub suppression toggle on test pool to see if reducing background scrubs reduces event correlation. Risk: may mask true issue; short windows only. Owner: Leah. Start: 2027-07-23.
E) NVLink low-level replay: use nvlink test harness to inject training sequences and long flits between GPUs while capturing link counters. Owner: SRE lab. Target: 2027-07-28.

Immediate mitigations for production (safe, reversible):
- Eviction policy: prefer preemptible placement to avoid tight colocation of heavy NVLink workloads on same PDU during nightly batch windows. Ops runbook updated.
- Rolling driver bump trial on Dedicated pool green lane (non-critical) -> candidate rollout to 10% node subset with stricter restart monitoring.
- Increase syslog persistence: mount /var/log on separate persistent partition for nodes in affected racks to prevent log loss on reboot.

Data collection checklist (what to capture on next incident):
- Full /var/log/journal/syslog snapshot (pre/post) with timestamps 
- dmesg (copy early-printk buffer)
- nvlink counters from nvidia-smi dmon + nvlink counters in debugfs (before and after)
- ECC counters: baseline + delta over last 24h
- BMC/IPMI event logs and PDU telemetry for 5 minutes before event
- Running processes and GPUs attached (container list, cgroups)
- GPU firmware versions + driver versions + kernel version + bios revision

Bisect plan details (how we'll meaningfully reduce hypothesis space):
1) Control variables: keep OS kernel image and bios constant across nodes in test pool; vary only driver and PDU power conditions.
2) Metrics: resets per 1k GPU-hours; mean time to first reset; median ECC correctable rate during run.
3) Stat target: detect 2x increase in reset rate with p<0.05 across variants (may need weeks of data, so use accelerated stress).
4) Stop criteria: if a variant shows clear improvement (>=50% reduction and reproducible), consider staged rollout and escalate to firmware vendor.

Open questions / unknowns (for follow-up):
- Is there a firmware-level known issue for the retimer chips on these rev batches? (hardware team to confirm ASINs).
- Is our syslog/ringbuffer configuration losing critical pre-crash traces? Need to improve collection across fleet.
- Are there other co-located workloads that cause power spikes (e.g., one-off internal jobs)? We need cross-team scheduling visibility.

Notes from oncall shifts (verbatim short logs):
- "2027-07-11 03:14 UTC: node-a09-gpu17 dropped, no oops, BMC says 3.4s loss of management connectivity. rebooted by watchdog. user job retried."
- "2027-07-13 21:02 UTC: dmesg shows nvlink: timeout waiting for peer, driver: ctx->free null pointer at free_mem+0x3c"
- "2027-07-16 00:42 UTC: heavy batch run on a10 PDU-2; three nodes in same PDU had small ECC spikes; one reset."

Action items (owners & due):
- Diego: spin up test pool with netconsole and persistent early_printk (due 2027-07-20).
- Priya: schedule PDU power-injection experiment with hardware ops (due 2027-07-24).
- Ethan: prepare driver images and roll plan (due 2027-07-21).
- Leah: add runbook snippets for oncall to capture netconsole and IPMI logs (due 2027-07-22).
- Hardware: list affected node serials and retimer revision (due 2027-07-25).

Appendix: useful commands and locations
- Collect dmesg and last kmsg: sudo journalctl -k -b -1 || sudo cp /var/log/dmesg /tmp/dmesg-$(date +%s)
- nvlink counters: sudo nvidia-smi nvlink --status; sudo cat /sys/kernel/debug/nvlink/*/stats
- ECC counters: sudo nvidia-smi -q -d MIG,ERR; parse Field "Correctable ECC Errors"
- Netconsole setup (quick): sudo modprobe netconsole netconsole=@src-host/eth0,@collector/6666
- IPMI: ipmitool sel elist; ipmitool sol activate for serial logs

Quick log excerpts (sanitized stack):
- [ 12345.678901] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: gpu_watchdog: thread stuck for 1234s
- [ 12345.679012] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: nvlink: handshake timeout peer id 0x02
- [ 12345.680001] kernel: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#2 stuck for 23s

Summary (one-liner):
Ghost resets are intermittent multi-causal events — likely a conjunction of power/colocation stress + edge-case driver/firmware behavior under NVLink-heavy loads. Next week we run controlled bisect experiments and improve telemetry capture to either isolate a firmware/hardware root cause or validate a driver fix.

-- Leah
